title: Bloomberg launches enterprise MCP for AI data access
key_facts: Bloomberg launched Bloomberg Enterprise Model Context Protocol (MCP) for its licensed-data service, giving clients' AI agents access to licensed Bloomberg data through a standard interface.
The layer covers more than 100 million securities and more than 50,000 fields.
Each field comes with metadata saying what it means, how it was calculated and when it applies, such as currency, price type and as-of date.

Agents can find fields and securities with natural-language search; Bloomberg also adds reusable workflow functions it calls Skills, such as spotting outliers, reviewing trades that breach price-deviation limits and checking sanctions exposure.
Requests are checked against a client's entitlements before any data is returned; Bloomberg hosts the service and clients keep control of their own agents and models.
Tony McManus, Bloomberg's global head of enterprise data and indices, says the bottleneck for financial institutions has shifted from model capability to data readiness.
Offered as an enterprise product to existing data-licence clients.
quote_evidence: The new access layer covers more than 100 million securities and more than 50,000 fields.
Requests are checked against a client's entitlements before any data is returned, and tool-level limits restrict the number of securities and fields in a single call.
Enterprise MCP is being offered as an enterprise product for Data Licence clients, with access governed under existing Bloomberg data rights.
why_it_matters_hint: Banks and asset managers using AI agents get a permission-checked, labelled route to Bloomberg data.
event_date: Reported 13 Oct 2026 (08:30 UTC); date of Bloomberg's own release not seen
notes: IT Brief UK relays Bloomberg's announcement; I could not find the Bloomberg press release (bloomberg.com press page returned 403), so the entry says "IT Brief UK reports, citing Bloomberg". A sister site, IT Brief Australia, carries the same headline later on 13 Oct. Launch date may be 12 or 13 Oct.
